tasks.prompt: Order the steps to establish a new district metered area in an Ontario distribution system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario system creating a new DMA from an existing pressure zone with boundary valves and one inlet meter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning through commissioning of the DMA boundary and inlet metering.

cards.label: Verify isolation by checking for zero flow with the inlet closed overnight
Close and tag boundary valves to isolate the DMA except at the planned inlet
Install the inlet flow meter and pressure logger at the single feed point
Commission continuous inlet flow and pressure recording and set the reporting baseline
Define DMA boundaries using pipe network maps and natural pressure zone limits

tasks.explanation: Boundaries must be defined first, then the area is isolated, metered, proven isolated by a zero flow check, and only then commissioned for routine monitoring.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to select a DMA size and layout for leakage management.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA design study using customer counts and network records.
tasks.configuration: Scope: desktop design before any field work begins.

cards.label: Confirm boundary valves exist or can be installed at each closure point
Check that each candidate area can be fed through one or two metered inlets
Review customer counts, pipe ages, and historic break records for candidate areas
Finalize the DMA layout and record it on the system map
Group connections into areas of a manageable size for night flow comparison

tasks.explanation: Records review informs grouping, grouping must then be checked for metered inlets and closable boundaries before the layout can be finalized.

tasks.prompt: Order the boundary valve proving steps before a DMA goes live.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional field crew proving DMA boundary valves during daytime low demand.
tasks.configuration: Scope: boundary valve location through drop test confirmation.

cards.label: Open the single inlet and record stable DMA pressure
Exercise each boundary valve to confirm it opens and closes fully
Close all boundary valves to isolate the DMA
Locate each boundary valve from records and mark it in the field
Close the inlet briefly and confirm DMA pressure drops as expected

tasks.explanation: Valves must be found and proven operable before isolation, and the pressure drop test only means something once the area is isolated and fed from one inlet.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to install a DMA inlet meter chamber.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional inlet meter installation on a 300 mm main with a planned shutdown, traffic control in place.
tasks.configuration: Scope: shutdown through return to service.

cards.label: Isolate and drain the work section and confirm zero pressure
Cut in the chamber and set the meter with correct flow direction
Refill slowly, vent air, and disinfect the new section before opening
Restore flow and compare meter readings against expected demand
Notify affected customers and confirm the planned shutdown window

tasks.explanation: Notification and isolation precede cutting in, disinfection precedes return to service, and reading checks close the job.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to validate DMA inlet meter data in the first month.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA with one month of 15 minute inlet flow data and known meter accuracy limits.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw data review through acceptance of the baseline.

cards.label: Accept the validated month as the DMA performance baseline
Investigate and explain any period where the balance does not close
Compare totalized DMA inflow with treatment plant output for the same period
Check the logger clock and interval settings against the recording standard
Screen the data for gaps, spikes, and flatlined periods

tasks.explanation: Logger settings are checked first, data quality screening follows, system level comparison comes next, discrepancies are explained, and only then is a baseline accepted.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to investigate a DMA with suddenly rising inflow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA where weekly average inflow rose with no new connections added.
tasks.configuration: Scope: office review through field confirmation.

cards.label: Review recent boundary valve work that could have opened a boundary
Compare the rise against weather, season, and known large user activity
Confirm the rise is real by checking the meter and logger for faults
Carry out a night flow check to see if the rise persists at minimum demand
Inspect the DMA for visible leakage or unauthorized use indicated by the checks

tasks.explanation: Meter faults are ruled out first, legitimate demand changes are considered next, boundary integrity is reviewed, night flow narrows the cause, and field inspection acts on the findings.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to split an oversized DMA into two smaller areas.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA proving too large for sensitive night flow analysis, split along a trunk main.
tasks.configuration: Scope: analysis through commissioning of both new areas.

cards.label: Identify the new boundary valves and the second inlet meter location
Prove isolation of each new area with separate zero flow checks
Analyse night flow records to choose a split line that balances both areas
Install the second inlet meter and close the new boundary valves
Begin separate night flow reporting for each new DMA

tasks.explanation: The split line comes from data analysis, hardware and boundaries follow, each area is proven separately, and reporting starts only after both are proven.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to add pressure logging to an existing DMA.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA with flow metering already in place, adding inlet and critical point pressure loggers.
tasks.configuration: Scope: site selection through first data review.

cards.label: Review pressure ranges against the zone target band
Select the inlet point and the highest and lowest critical points in the DMA
Install calibrated pressure loggers and record exact elevations
Synchronize logger clocks with the flow logger
Collect at least one full week including a weekend

tasks.explanation: Points are selected by elevation and hydraulics first, loggers are installed and synchronized, a representative week is collected, and review closes the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to retire a temporary DMA used for a leakage study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional temporary DMA created for a three month leakage study that is now complete.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study closeout through records update.

cards.label: Notify operations staff that the area has returned to normal configuration
Remove DMA tags and update the system map and valve records
Complete and file the final leakage study report
Reopen boundary valves to restore the normal network configuration
Remove temporary loggers and download their final data

tasks.explanation: The study is closed first, equipment is removed, the network is restored, records are corrected, and staff are notified of the restored configuration.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to brief a contractor before DMA boundary work.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional contractor hired to replace two DMA boundary valves under utility supervision.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pre work briefing through site handover.

cards.label: Hand over the site with the utility operator retaining control of valve operation
Confirm shutdown notifications and traffic control responsibilities
Review which valves must stay closed to protect DMA isolation
Issue the contractor the DMA map showing boundary valves and flow direction
Walk the site and confirm valve locations and chamber access

tasks.explanation: Maps and isolation rules come first, responsibilities are confirmed next, the site is walked, and handover keeps valve control with the utility.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to hand over a distribution emergency to the next shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ongoing trunk break repair crossing a shift change at midnight.
tasks.configuration: Scope: log review through incoming crew deployment.

cards.label: Summarize isolated valves, affected customers, and estimated repair time in the log
Confirm which samples are pending and who owns each result follow up
Record the handover with both supervisors names and the time
Walk the site together if conditions allow a safe joint inspection
Brief the incoming supervisor on site conditions, risks, and pending notifications

tasks.explanation: The log summary comes first, briefing follows, pending samples and ownership are confirmed, a joint site walk transfers local knowledge, and the signed handover record closes the transfer.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a minimum night flow study in an established DMA.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA study during the typical lowest demand window on a dry weather night.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparation through calculation of net night flow.

cards.label: Select the minimum one hour average flow as the minimum night flow
Record inlet flow at short intervals through the night low demand window
Confirm boundary valves are closed and the DMA is fed only through the inlet meter
Note any known legitimate night use by large customers in the DMA
Subtract assessed legitimate night use to obtain net night flow for leakage assessment

tasks.explanation: Isolation is confirmed first, flow is recorded, legitimate use is documented, the minimum hour is selected, and net night flow is calculated last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to assess legitimate night use in a DMA.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA with homes, a hospital, and one 24 hour industrial customer.
tasks.configuration: Scope: customer review through the legitimate night use allowance.

cards.label: Apply the standard household night use allowance per occupied property
Add continuous process use confirmed with the customer
Meter or obtain records for large continuous night users
List all non household customers inside the DMA boundary
Record the total legitimate night use used in leakage calculations

tasks.explanation: Customers are listed first, large users are measured directly, household allowance is applied, confirmed process use is added, and the total is recorded for use in calculations.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a step test to locate leakage within a DMA.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional step test carried out at night with crews at sectional valves and a logger at the inlet.
tasks.configuration: Scope: setup through identification of the leaking section.

cards.label: Divide the DMA into sections that can be isolated one at a time from the far end
Station crews with radios at each sectional valve
Work toward the inlet, closing one section at a time and recording each drop
Close the farthest section valve and record the inlet flow drop
Flag the section with the largest unexplained flow drop for leak detection follow up

tasks.explanation: Sections are planned first, crews are stationed, sections are closed in sequence from the far end, and the largest drop identifies where leak detection goes next.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to trend DMA night flow over a season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operations review comparing weekly net night flow across a summer season.
tasks.configuration: Scope: data preparation through management reporting.

cards.label: Investigate any sustained rise that events do not explain
Validate each week of inlet flow data and remove logger fault periods
Plot the trend and mark known events such as main breaks and flushing
Calculate weekly net night flow using the same legitimate use allowance
Report the seasonal leakage trend and recommended actions

tasks.explanation: Data is validated first, a consistent calculation follows, events are marked on the trend, unexplained rises are investigated, and reporting closes the review.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to respond to a single night of abnormally high night flow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA showing one night with flow well above its normal minimum.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm review through closeout.

cards.label: Check boundary valve records for any operation that night
Record the finding and close or escalate the alarm with reasons
If unexplained, schedule a repeat night check before raising a leak investigation
Check operations logs for flushing, filling, or break repairs that night
Check the logger and meter for faults or a clock shift

tasks.explanation: Equipment faults and known operations are checked before assuming leakage, a repeat check confirms persistence, and the alarm is closed or escalated with documented reasons.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to convert night flow findings into a leak detection work plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility prioritizing three DMAs with rising net night flow.
tasks.configuration: Scope: ranking through crew scheduling.

cards.label: Schedule night step testing followed by daytime sounding and correlation
Divide the worst DMA into step test sections
Set a post repair night flow target to verify savings
Rank DMAs by net night flow per kilometre of main and per connection
Confirm the worst DMA boundary integrity with a zero flow check

tasks.explanation: Ranking comes first, boundary integrity is confirmed, the area is sectioned, field work is scheduled in sequence, and a verification target is set before work begins.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to verify leakage savings after DMA repairs.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA where two leaks found by step testing have been repaired.
tasks.configuration: Scope: post repair monitoring through savings report.

cards.label: Report verified savings and update the DMA baseline
Measure minimum night flow over at least three comparable nights
Allow the DMA to settle for several normal demand nights after repairs
Calculate net night flow with the same legitimate use allowance as before
Compare with the pre repair baseline to quantify the reduction

tasks.explanation: Settling comes first, comparable nights are measured, the same calculation method is used, comparison quantifies savings, and the baseline is updated last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to prepare a DMA for winter night flow comparison.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario DMA where summer irrigation distorts night flow comparison.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal planning through winter baseline setting.

cards.label: Identify the summer period when irrigation inflates night use
Measure minimum night flow through the selected window
Set the winter baseline used for year over year leakage comparison
Select a stable cold weather window with no flushing or construction
Confirm large winter night users such as arena plants with the customers

tasks.explanation: Distorted periods are identified first, a clean window is chosen, winter users are confirmed, flow is measured, and the baseline is set from that measurement.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to create a new pressure zone in a growing subdivision area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario system where growth at higher elevation causes low pressure complaints in an existing zone.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study through commissioning of the new zone.

cards.label: Close and tag the boundary valves between the two zones
Verify pressures at critical points in both zones and record the new zone settings
Install a PRV feed or booster feed for the new higher zone
Set the new zone boundary along streets where valves can separate the zones
Model or calculate zone pressures at peak hour using ground elevations and head loss

tasks.explanation: Hydraulics are worked out first, the boundary follows the hydraulics, the feed is installed, zones are separated, and verification closes the work.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a PRV annual inspection and service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional pressure reducing valve station on a scheduled annual service, bypass available.
tasks.configuration: Scope: isolation through return to service.

cards.label: Record inlet and outlet pressures before disturbing the station
Inspect the main valve and pilot system for wear, debris, and corrosion
Return the PRV to service, reset the outlet pressure, and record final settings
Clean strainers and replace worn soft parts as needed
Isolate the PRV and open the bypass under controlled pressure

tasks.explanation: Baseline pressures are recorded first, isolation and bypass follow, inspection and servicing come next, and reset with records closes the service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to lower DMA pressure to reduce leakage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional DMA with high average pressure and pressure dependent leakage, critical point monitored.
tasks.configuration: Scope: assessment through post change monitoring.

cards.label: Confirm the critical point pressure at peak demand and the margin above the minimum standard
Hold the lowest setting that keeps the critical point above the minimum at peak
Monitor critical point and customer complaints after each step
Reduce the PRV outlet setting in small steps during low risk hours
Compare night flow before and after to confirm leakage reduction

tasks.explanation: The available margin is confirmed first, reductions are gradual and monitored, the safe lowest setting is held, and night flow comparison confirms the benefit.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to investigate low pressure complaints in one neighbourhood.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional cluster of low pressure complaints on one street during morning peak.
tasks.configuration: Scope: complaint review through cause confirmation.

cards.label: Install temporary pressure loggers at a complainant service and a nearby hydrant
Compare logged pressures with zone targets during the complaint window
Confirm the cause, such as a partly closed valve or undersized main, before planning the fix
Check system pressures and recent valve or PRV changes in the area
Map the complaints by location, time of day, and elevation

tasks.explanation: Complaint patterns are mapped first, recent system changes are checked, field logging measures the problem, comparison tests the targets, and cause confirmation precedes any fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to investigate high pressure complaints and fixture damage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional low lying street with repeated plumbing fixture failures near a zone boundary.
tasks.configuration: Scope: complaint review through corrective setting change.

cards.label: Check the PRV outlet setting and recent service records for the feeding station
Recheck pressures at the property and record the corrected settings
Confirm service pressures with a gauge at an affected property
Log pressure over 24 hours to capture night time peaks when demand is low
Reduce the PRV setting or repair the pilot if control has failed

tasks.explanation: Pressures are confirmed first, the feeding PRV is checked, logging captures night peaks, correction follows the evidence, and rechecking verifies the fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to commission a new PRV station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional new PRV station installed between a high zone and a low zone, construction complete.
tasks.configuration: Scope: flushing through handover to operations.

cards.label: Test the station response by varying downstream demand
Set the pilot to the design outlet pressure with the station on bypass control
Flush the station piping and confirm strainers are clean
Open the station slowly and watch downstream pressure stabilize
Record final settings, tag the station, and hand over records to operations

tasks.explanation: Clean piping comes first, the pilot is preset, the station is opened slowly, response is tested, and records and handover close commissioning.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to respond to a failed PRV causing downstream overpressure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional PRV failed open at night, downstream pressures rising toward fixture damage levels.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm through post incident review.

cards.label: Notify affected customers if pressures exceeded safe plumbing levels
Close the upstream isolation valve or throttle the bypass to control pressure
Confirm downstream pressure from the logger and a field gauge reading
Restore normal settings, verify pressures, and complete an incident record
Remove and repair or replace the failed valve and pilot parts

tasks.explanation: Confirmation comes first, pressure is controlled, customers are notified, the valve is repaired, and restoration with documentation closes the incident.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to set seasonal PRV settings for a zone with a large arena load.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone where winter arena ice making raises peak demand compared with summer.
tasks.configuration: Scope: demand review through seasonal changeover.

cards.label: Review logged peak demands and critical point pressures for both seasons
Adjust the pilot setting and verify critical point pressure under load
Schedule the changeover for a low demand period and notify operations staff
Record the seasonal settings and the dates they apply in the station log
Calculate the outlet setting needed to hold the critical point minimum in each season

tasks.explanation: Seasonal evidence is reviewed first, settings are calculated, changeover is scheduled and staff notified, the adjustment is verified under load, and the log is updated last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a pressure survey of an entire pressure zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone wide pressure survey using hydrant loggers over one week.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning through reporting.

cards.label: Report problem areas and recommend PRV or main improvements
Compare results with the hydraulic expectations and zone targets
Record pressures for a full week including the peak demand day
Calibrate loggers and synchronize clocks before deployment
Select logger sites covering high, low, and far points of the zone

tasks.explanation: Site selection comes first, calibration precedes deployment, a representative week is recorded, results are compared with targets, and recommendations close the survey.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to manage pressure transients after a booster pump trip.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional booster station trip that sent a pressure wave through a zone with air valves and a surge vessel.
tasks.configuration: Scope: event review through protective changes.

cards.label: Record the event analysis and the settings changed
Adjust pump start and stop ramping or surge settings to soften future trips
Download pump and pressure records to reconstruct the trip event
Inspect air valves and the surge vessel for correct operation
Check for customer damage reports and main breaks in the affected zone

tasks.explanation: The event is reconstructed first, surge equipment is inspected, damage is checked, controls are adjusted, and the analysis is recorded last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to prepare an elevated tank for internal inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional elevated tank taken out of service for a scheduled internal inspection, system demand met by other storage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning through safe entry readiness.

cards.label: Notify customers and the fire department of the temporary storage change
Drain the tank in a controlled way that protects the receiving drainage
Set up ventilation, lighting, and confined space entry controls at the access hatch
Test the atmosphere and issue the entry permit before anyone enters
Confirm other storage and pumping can meet demand while the tank is out

tasks.explanation: Supply is secured first, stakeholders are notified, draining follows, entry controls are set up, and atmospheric testing and the permit come immediately before entry.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps during an internal tank inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional inspector inside a drained steel tank with a surface attendant and rescue plan in place.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entry through inspection reporting.

cards.label: Photograph defects and prepare the inspection report with repair priorities
Enter under the confined space permit with continuous atmospheric monitoring
Check ladders, vents, screens, and the overflow for condition and security
Measure and record sediment depth across the floor
Inspect roof, walls, and floor coatings for failure and corrosion

tasks.explanation: Entry under permit comes first, structure and coating are inspected, appurtenances are checked, sediment is measured, and documented reporting closes the inspection.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to clean and disinfect a ground storage reservoir.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ground reservoir removed from service for cleaning after sediment was found at inspection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: isolation through return to service.

cards.label: Isolate and drain the reservoir and confirm zero inflow
Remove sediment and wash interior surfaces without damaging coatings
Disinfect interior surfaces using the approved chlorination method for storage facilities
Return the reservoir to service only after satisfactory sample results
Refill and hold, then sample for bacteriological quality and chlorine residual

tasks.explanation: Isolation and draining come first, cleaning precedes disinfection, refilling and sampling follow, and satisfactory results are required before return to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to return a tank to service after coating repairs.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank where interior coating repairs have cured and the contractor has demobilized.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cure verification through normal operation.

cards.label: Clean and disinfect the interior following the storage disinfection procedure
Verify coating cure time and inspect the repair for holidays and adhesion
Collect bacteriological samples and confirm chlorine residual after filling
Fill slowly and check the exterior and fittings for leaks
Place the tank in normal level control and record the return to service

tasks.explanation: Cure and repair quality are verified first, disinfection follows, filling checks for leaks, sampling confirms safety, and normal control resumes last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an external tank inspection from the ground and roof.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional annual external inspection of a standpipe that stays in service.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparation through work order creation.

cards.label: Create work orders ranked by risk for every defect found
Inspect the foundation, shell, and paint condition from the ground
Check the overflow discharge and screen for blockage or damage
Access the roof under fall protection and inspect the vent, hatch, and roof coating
Review the previous inspection report and known defect list

tasks.explanation: History is reviewed first, ground inspection follows, roof inspection comes next under fall protection, the overflow is checked, and ranked work orders close the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to investigate a tank overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional elevated tank that overflowed at night, level telemetry available.
tasks.configuration: Scope: event confirmation through corrective action.

cards.label: Correct the control fault and test the high level alarm and shutoff
Record the event, water loss estimate, and corrective actions
Review level control and altitude valve operation during the event
Check whether a pump or PRV change filled the tank beyond its normal band
Confirm the overflow from telemetry and a site visit checking for erosion or ice

tasks.explanation: Confirmation comes first, controls are reviewed, contributing changes are checked, the fault is corrected and alarms tested, and documentation closes the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to schedule tank cleaning across a multi tank system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional utility with six tanks setting a multi year cleaning and inspection rotation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inventory through published schedule.

cards.label: Publish the multi year schedule with budget estimates for each year
Rank tanks by sediment load, water age risk, and time since last cleaning
Check seasonal demand so no tank is cleaned during peak season or fire risk periods
Compile each tank age, coating history, sediment findings, and water quality role
Build the rotation so only one tank is out of service at a time

tasks.explanation: Inventory comes first, risk ranking follows, seasonal constraints are applied, the one at a time rotation is built, and the funded schedule is published last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to drain a tank safely for winter in a seasonal system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional seasonal campground system tank drained each fall under Ontario practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: shutdown notice through secured empty tank.

cards.label: Open vents and hatches as designed for winter and secure them against entry
Notify seasonal customers of the shutdown date and final use day
Drain and flush low points and protect the discharge from erosion
Stop inflow and use or discharge stored water in a controlled manner
Record the drained condition and the spring recommissioning tasks

tasks.explanation: Notice comes first, stored water is handled in a controlled way, draining protects the site, the tank is secured for winter, and recommissioning tasks are recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to inspect tank mixing and stratification with the tank in service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional in service inspection using a remote camera and water quality profiling, no entry and no draining.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning through findings report.

cards.label: Report stratification and condition findings with recommended actions
Inspect interior surfaces visible to the camera for coating and sediment
Review level records to plan profiling at full and low levels
Lower a disinfected camera and sampling line through the roof hatch
Profile temperature and chlorine residual at several depths

tasks.explanation: Level planning comes first, disinfected equipment is lowered, depth profiling measures stratification, camera inspection covers condition, and reporting closes the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to respond to ice damage found on a tank roof vent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional winter inspection finding a crushed vent screen and ice buildup at the roof hatch.
tasks.configuration: Scope: finding through verified repair.

cards.label: Check the hatch seal and interior for any contamination entry during the damage period
Record the repair and add vent checks to the winter inspection round
Replace the damaged vent and screen with the approved assembly
Restrict roof access until ice conditions are safe to work in
Assess whether the vent still protects the tank from contamination

tasks.explanation: Safe access comes first, protective function is assessed, the vent is replaced, contamination entry is checked, and records plus preventive checks close the response.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to diagnose poor turnover in a storage tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank whose level varies only slightly each day, with falling outlet chlorine residual.
tasks.configuration: Scope: records review through confirmed diagnosis.

cards.label: Check inlet and outlet arrangement for short circuiting between them
Profile temperature and residual with depth to detect stratification
Confirm the diagnosis, such as low daily draw or inlet outlet short circuiting
Calculate daily exchange volume from level records as a share of tank volume
Compare water age indicators with tanks that turn over well

tasks.explanation: Exchange volume is quantified first, profiling tests for stratification, piping arrangement is checked, comparison supports the finding, and diagnosis is confirmed last.
